response: Yes, confined placental mosaicism (CPM) has been associated with adverse perinatal outcomes in IVF pregnancies. CPM occurs when there is a mixture of normal and abnormal cells in the placenta, but not in the fetus. This condition can lead to complications such as intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), low birth weight, and preterm birth, which are common adverse perinatal outcomes in IVF pregnancies. Studies have suggested that CPM may be more frequent in IVF pregnancies due to the assisted reproductive technology (ART) process, and it is considered a potential contributor to the increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes observed in these pregnancies.
